Each stage—data understanding, problem definition, planning, execution, reporting, and refinement—acts as a checkpoint for validation and revision. This structure enables a dual-layered reasoning process: one grounded in computational logic (LLM-driven), and another rooted in domain-specific judgment (human expert). The iterative nature ensures that errors propagate minimally and can be corrected systematically. From a mathematical standpoint, this resembles a Bayesian hierarchical model where each stage updates posterior distributions conditioned on prior beliefs and new evidence. The control points ensure that these updates are inspectable and verifiable, aligning with principles of conformal prediction and causal inference. The breakdown regime arises when either the AI fails to capture domain nuances or the human expert bypasses necessary checks, resulting in flawed conclusions.
